title: Ikigai
author: Héctor García and Francesc Miralles
blurb: Why do so many people on the Japanese island of Okinawa live past 100, and stay cheerful doing it? Héctor García and Francesc Miralles set out to find out, visiting the rural village of Ogimi and talking with its oldest residents. Their answer centres on ikigai, a Japanese idea that roughly means your reason for getting up in the morning. The book blends those interviews with everyday habits and ideas from psychology. It covers eating until you are about 80 percent full, moving gently every day, and staying close to friends and community. It draws on Viktor Frankl's logotherapy and Japanese Morita therapy to explore meaning, and on the idea of flow to show how absorbing activities keep us engaged. It ends with resilience, embracing imperfection, and ten simple rules for living a long, purposeful life.

lessons.t: Find Your Reason to Get Up
lessons.b: Ikigai is the personal sense of purpose that gives each day meaning, and the authors argue it is linked to living longer and happier.
issues: scene 6: The 'MY FOUR CIRCLES' notebook label overlaps the outline of the top 'LOVE' circle. The circle stroke cuts through the word 'CIRCLES'. (fix: Move the label higher (e.g. ~30px further up into the notebook's top margin), or shift the Venn diagram down/right so the top circle clears the label.)

lessons.b: In Ogimi, the oldest residents stay busy, tend their gardens and belong to close-knit support groups called moai, showing that community and daily purpose go hand in hand.
issues: scene 5: The bottom-right caption 'Nobody faces life alone.' sits almost directly on top of the 'visualgrowth.app' brand mark. The two text blocks nearly touch, and the caption crowds the bottom edge. (fix: Move the circle diagram and its caption up about 40px, or shrink the circle slightly, so the caption ends well above the brand mark (at least 30px clear).)

lessons.b: The Okinawan habit of hara hachi bu, stopping before you are full and eating a varied, plant-rich diet, is one simple pillar of a long life.

Push the 'EVERY MEAL' row and its label further down, or left-align the label with clear vertical spacing (about 24px or more) between the two.)

scene 6: On the right scale pan, the coloured dots spill past the pan's right edge, so the drawing looks broken. (fix: Shrink the dots or tighten their spacing so all four fit inside the pan's outline.)

lessons.b: Fully absorbing yourself in a challenging activity you enjoy creates flow, and seeking flow in work and hobbies is a practical path toward your ikigai.
Logotherapy helps you discover what gives your life meaning, while Morita therapy teaches you to accept your emotions and act purposefully anyway.
